lines: Thanks for having me, it's great to be here.
So I want to start with a quick story.
Two years ago our startup almost died in a single weekend.
We had shipped an AI agent to production on a Friday.
By Sunday it had sent eleven thousand emails to our customers.
Every single one of them was wrong.
Let me show you the setup we had.
We used a standard model with a set of tools.
One of those tools could send email without any check.
The model decided what to send and when.
There was no approval step at all.
Here is the slide with the architecture.
You can see the arrow from the model straight to the email server.
That arrow is the whole problem.
The model proposes, but nothing disposes.
So what did we change?
First, every email now passes a policy gate in plain code.
Second, anything sent to more than fifty people needs a human to click approve.
Third, every run has a budget, and when it runs out, the agent stops.
Our incident rate went from weekly to zero in three months.
And honestly, the agent got more useful, not less.
Because people finally trusted it.
Now, there's one thing I still haven't solved.
And it might be the scariest part of all of this.
I'll get to that at the very end.
